plain_description.what: Runs the production judge recipe (same reference answers, mechanics and rubric) with a different judge model family, grok, on 1,980 matches. It compares the result with grok's old-recipe verdicts and with the Mistral judge. About 4k calls.
plain_description.why: It asks whether the judge's accuracy gain comes from the recipe or from the particular judge model (Mistral).
plain_description.information: If grok gains as much, the recipe carries the gain and cheaper or other judges can be swapped in. Result: done, passed. Accuracy is 0.864 with the recipe against 0.744 without it, and 0.722 against 0.568 on the top cluster. This is nearly identical to Mistral (0.865 / 0.699) and gives the same leaderboard. A later cell-level check found per-subject gaps of at most 3.2 points, each with an interval that includes zero. Under this recipe the judge model accounts for only about 3% of committed verdicts. Older judged question family, later ruled 'history, not evidence'.
